items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions Andre Hodler's book and观点; Interviewee does not respond to the mention of Hodler specifically, only to the musical description.

ctx.x: Jazzy, yeah, yeah. Maybe, you know. But yes, Boyd Centa was all over.
There's one thing maybe I can get your reaction to, and that is that in his book, "Jazz -- It's Evolution and Essence", Andre Hodler makes quite a

point that you were one ... now I don't want to overstate this, but one of, perhaps we would call it, a vanguard of younger musicians in the twenties, who -- with a certain kind of instrumental sound, a certain attention to what you might call a more delicate, more refined, or elegant style of playing, an attention to perhaps a more legitimate kind of articulation and vibrato and so forth, offered, as he describes a reaction to, and I think that I'm quoting him -- what he calls the "violently colored sonority of…
